title: TCP/IP Protocol Suite
markdown:
The **TCP/IP Protocol Suite** is the standard communication framework used by the Internet. Designed prior to the OSI model, TCP/IP originally specified four layers, commonly compared as a **5-layer model** when mapped against OSI.

### Comparing TCP/IP and OSI

| OSI Model | TCP/IP Protocol Suite | Key Protocols |
|---|---|---|
| **Application, Presentation, Session** | **Application Layer** | HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS, SNMP, SSH |
| **Transport Layer** | **Transport Layer** | TCP, UDP, SCTP |
| **Network Layer** | **Network (Internet) Layer** | IP, ICMP, IGMP, ARP, RARP (obsolete) |
| **Data Link Layer** | **Link Layer** | Ethernet, Wi-Fi (802.11), PPP |
| **Physical Layer** | **Physical Layer** | Copper wire, Fiber optics, Radio |

### Core Protocols

- **TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)** — Connection-oriented, reliable protocol that divides data into segments, tracks sequence numbers, and requests retransmission for lost packets.
- **IP (Internet Protocol)** — Unreliable, connectionless protocol responsible for logical addressing and routing packets across intermediate networks.
- **UDP (User Datagram Protocol)** — Lightweight, fast, connectionless protocol without flow control or guaranteed delivery.
